Ej.bar_b_note: A's deeper teal back over a pale chest gives the otter form and a readable silhouette, but the neutral grey stage carries no Valheim-class light or atmosphere, and B's uniform saturated cyan reads as plastic.

Kt.bar_b_note: The blue-and-copper finned serpent has a strong colour identity, but its spiky, busy silhouette turns into a blue scribble at small size, and the bare stage gives it no world light.

Gj.bar_b_note: The warm earth-and-moss costume fits the Meadows palette, but the big-eyed animated-film face belongs to a different style family from the naturalistic creatures and trainer.

Rc.bar_b_note: The mossy plated shell and grounded anatomy are close to the style bar, but on a neutral stage nothing shows Palworld-class world finish or Valheim-class light.

Hv.bar_b_note: A matches the owner's Tanglevolt bar (indigo fur, white muzzle, readable rear and faint), but B's faint frames break into a black-and-white patchwork material, and the stage has no atmosphere either way.

Zx.bar_b_note: The Meadows sky, warm grass and blue mountain distance carry some mood, but the wall stands alone as a single panel next to a faceted pale boulder, and the flat grade and sparse lighting are not Valheim-class.

Mn.bar_b_note: The tan winged lion reads as a stock statue-like asset that matches no board, stands at an outsized scale against the tiny trainer, and has faint frames that stay half-upright, so it never reads as Tetherbound.

Ey.bar_b_note: The armoured boar has a strong, heavy silhouette, but the faint frames go near-black and float above a detached shadow, B's red lava seams and red tusks drift toward the reserved danger red, and the stage carries no world light.

top_changes.change: Fix the creature faint and hit-react materials, lighting and grounding: Hv B's faint frames swap to a black/white patchwork material; Ey's faint frames turn near-black and lift off a detached shadow; Kt A's and Mn B's hit reacts need a grounded flinch; Mn and Rc A need faint-end poses that lie down.

Ship Zx side A's homestead wall language everywhere (timber frame, diagonal brace, top cap, separate stone footing), and give it real thickness, a warmer and less bright infill, and neighbouring wall segments so it reads as part of a built homestead.
Replace the off-roster winged lion (Mn) with a roster creature at a sensible scale, and bring the villager face (Gj) into line with the naturalistic creature and trainer style.
